title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page completes §8, 'Les groupes N_σ, N_σ^♮', of a long technical computation in the continuation of La Longue Marche, manuscript pp. 650bis–787. The setting is fixed on the previous page. There is a group (scheme) G_{ρ,σ} with a subgroup G^♮, and an element σ that generates L_σ ≅ (Z/4Z)_{S_0}. N_σ is the subgroup of sections u with u(σ) = σ^{ε_2(u)}, i.e. the normaliser of ⟨σ⟩ up to inversion. Z_σ is the centraliser of σ and SZ_σ its 'special' part. The composite N_σ^♮ → G* → O_12^* is a split epimorphism, giving semidirect decompositions (175). The previous page also has SZ_σ ≅ L_σ × SZ_σ^♮ (177), and SZ_σ^♮ is described as G^♮ ∩ Z_σ, in terms of a vector group M.

On this page Grothendieck computes SZ_σ^♮ explicitly (178). Write sections of M as x = a_0λ_0 + a_1λ_1, so M is rank 2 over G_a. σ acts on M by exchanging λ_0 and λ_1, so the fixed points of σ (the kernel of 1 − σ_M) are the x with a_0 = a_1. This gives the line {a(λ_0+λ_1)} ≅ G_a.

Combining with (177) gives (179): SZ_σ ≅ L_σ × G_a, whose neutral component is SZ_σ^♮ ≅ G_a. Hence there is an exact sequence 1 → G_a → N_σ^♮ → O_12^* (= γ_{ρ,σ}) → 1. Since it splits, (175), (177) and (179) give (180): N_σ^♮ ≅ O_12^* ⋉ G_a and N_σ ≅ O_12^* ⋉ (L_σ × G_a).

The actions are made explicit in (181):
- a unit μ in O_12^* acts on λ through the character χ: O_12^* → G_m, by λ ↦ χ(μ)λ;
- it acts on σ through the sign character ε_2: O_12^* → (±1)_{S_0}, by σ ↦ σ^{ε_2(μ)}.

The purpose is structural: these normalisers N_ρ, N_σ are then glued as fibre products over γ = O_12^* on the next page. That gluing defines the groups M_{ρ,σ} and Γ_{ρ,σ}, which appear to be algebraic or proalgebraic envelopes attached to the elliptic elements ρ, σ of SL_2(Z)-type groups. This is part of Grothendieck's study of Teichmüller-type groups in the Longue Marche.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The computation of ker(1−σ_M) is correct provided σ acts on M by swapping λ_0 and λ_1; that action is implicit here and is not justified on this page.

The identification SZ_σ^♮ = (SZ_σ)° (neutral component) is correct given SZ_σ ≅ L_σ × G_a with L_σ finite étale. Over a non-reduced base or in characteristic dividing 4 one would need care, which is not addressed.

ideas.what: Fixed-point subgroup of an involution swapping two basis vectors of a rank-2 vector group is a line G_a·(λ_0+λ_1)
ideas.modern_name: invariants of a permutation representation / centraliser computation

ideas.what: Normaliser of a finite cyclic subgroup expressed as a semidirect product O_12^* ⋉ (L_σ × G_a), with the action via characters χ and ε_2
ideas.modern_name: structure of normalisers of elliptic elements in an (pro)algebraic envelope of a Teichmüller-type group
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981), unpublished in this detail

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping inside a long technical computation: a fixed-point calculation in a rank-2 vector group and assembly of semidirect products. Nothing here would surprise a specialist on its own. Any interest lies in the global construction (M_{ρ,σ}, Γ_{ρ,σ}), which is set up on the following pages.
transcription_corrections: The superscript on SZ_σ and N_σ looks like a small double-headed arrow ('⇆'). It is rendered inconsistently in the transcriptions as 'S', '♮' or '⊊'; it is the same decoration throughout.
In (178), the struck-out text inside the braces is replaced by the interlinear 'a_0λ_0+a_1λ_1', and the condition reads 'a_0 = a_1'.
The crossed-out label before the exact sequence is '(180)', which was then reused for the isomorphisms below it.
The struck-out line above (181) reads 'μ(σ) = σ^{ε_2(μ)}'. It is then rewritten as the second line of (181).
